title: ReLiveGym: Evaluating Long-Lived Agents over Weeks of Replayed Reality
content:
Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence
  [Submitted on 30 Sep 2026]
    Title:ReLiveGym: Evaluating Long-Lived Agents over Weeks of Replayed Reality
View PDF
            Abstract:As large language model (LLM) agents become widely adopted, they are increasingly deployed for tasks that require persistent monitoring or recurring actions (e.g., market analysis). These agents are expected to operate unattended for days or weeks, act at the right timing, and adapt to the dynamic environment over time. These challenges are not fully captured in the existing long-horizon agent work, as they often consider a static environment that is not temporally changing. We introduce ReLiveGym, a diagnostic evaluation environment of long-lived tasks in which agents act sparsely over simulated weeks of chronologically replayed real-world news, market, and social-media streams. The tasks span diverse levels of time sensitivity, reasoning intensity, and recurrence. Across eight base language models, we investigate how model choice and harness design affect agent performance on such long-lived tasks. Our results show that how agents determine when to act arises as an important harness-design axis for long-lived tasks; and that the optimal design varies across tasks and sometimes model choices as well. We also evaluate how continuous learning from hindsight feedback affects performance and addresses failure modes observed in these long-lived tasks. These findings indicate model choice, action timing mechanism, and use of feedback as important considerations in the design of long-lived agents. Code: this https URL

report.summary: ReLiveGym benchmarks long-lived LLM agents on weeks of chronologically replayed real-world news, market, and social streams, revealing action timing and feedback as key design axes.
report.background: LLM agents are moving from one-shot prompts and static benchmarks toward persistent, unattended operation. Real deployments increasingly require agents to monitor markets, inboxes, or social feeds for days or weeks, act at the right moment, and adapt as conditions change. Yet most long-horizon agent evaluations use static environments that do not evolve over time, so they miss timing, recurrence, and drift. ReLiveGym was built to fill that gap: it replays real-world news, market, and social-media streams in chronological order, compressing weeks into a simulated timeline. The paper evaluates eight base language models and different agent harnesses, then studies continuous learning from hindsight feedback. Its goal is diagnostic: expose where long-lived agents fail before they are trusted in production.
key_points: ReLiveGym creates a diagnostic environment where agents act sparsely over simulated weeks of chronologically replayed real-world news, market data, and social streams. Rather than solving a single static task, agents must decide when to wake, whether to act, and how to adapt as events unfold. Tasks vary in time sensitivity, reasoning intensity, and recurrence, making timing a first-class challenge.

The study compares eight base language models and different harness designs. Results show that performance is not just about raw model quality: how the agent harness determines when to act emerges as a critical design axis. The best timing strategy varies by task and sometimes by model, so no single scheduling pattern dominates.

Continuous learning from hindsight feedback helps long-lived agents improve over the simulated weeks. It addresses failure modes observed in persistent tasks, such as missing time-sensitive events, acting too often, or failing to adjust after new information. This suggests memory and reflection loops are practical components, not optional extras.

The benchmark targets real-world recurring or monitoring jobs like market analysis, where unattended operation for days or weeks is expected. By replaying actual streams, it preserves temporal order and realistic noise. That makes evaluation closer to deployment conditions than static long-horizon benchmarks, while remaining reproducible.
report.impact: For the AI industry, ReLiveGym shifts evaluation from static question answering toward temporal autonomy: when an agent acts may matter as much as what it outputs. Agent framework builders will need better schedulers, event triggers, persistent memory, and feedback loops. Developers should treat timing policy, state management, and continuous learning as core architecture, not prompt afterthoughts. For regular users, the promise is more reliable always-on assistants for market alerts, inbox triage, and monitoring, but also new risks: missed time-sensitive events, stale or duplicate actions, drift, and unpredictable compute costs. Expect future agent benchmarks and products to emphasize weeks-long reliability rather than single-session wins.
report.tools: Follow the paper's code link for ReLiveGym. Related tools include agent frameworks with stateful graph orchestration such as LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI; long-term memory layers like Letta/MemGPT and Zep; streaming and scheduling systems such as Temporal and Airflow; and reflection or hindsight-learning libraries. For evaluation, pair these with time-ordered replay harnesses and event-triggered logging to measure when agents act, not only what they answer.
